question.text: If $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are two polynomials such that $\phi(x)=f\left(x^3\right)+x g\left(x^3\right)$ is divisible by $x^2+x+1$, then

options.text: none of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ is divisible by $(x-1)$
$g(x)$ is divisible by $(x-1)$ but $f(x)$ is not divisible by $(x-1)$
$f(x)$ is divisible by $(x-1)$ but $g(x)$ is not divisible by $(x-1)$

solution.text:
$\because$ By remainder theorom
$\begin{aligned}
& \phi(\omega)=0 \quad \& \phi\left(\omega^2\right)=0 \quad\left(\omega, \omega^2 \text { are complex cube root of unity }\right) \\
& \Rightarrow f(1)+\omega g(1)=0 \quad \& \quad f(1)+\omega^2 g(1)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow f(1)=g(1)=0 \\
& \therefore \phi(1)=f(1)+g(1)=0
\end{aligned}$
